issuer: the Naoero Revenue Office, with the approval of the Registrar under the Motor Traffic Act 2014
note: Read 2026-10-30 in RONLAW (ronlaw.gov.nr, the Republic's online legal database): the Motor Traffic Act 2014 and the Motor Traffic Regulations 2014 in their Service 6 consolidations (pages dated 30 September 2026, taking in Act 21 of 2026), whose text was read through RONLAW's own search service (the site renders the PDFs in a script viewer; the indexed page text was saved). Section 21: a person over 17 may apply for a learner's permit (up to a year). Section 22: after the practical test the Registrar issues an application for a driver's licence, taken to the Naoero Revenue Office for payment and issue. Section 26(1)(a): the Revenue Office, with the Registrar's approval, may grant a licence to a person not less than 18 who has completed a learner's test (or shows a foreign licence, s 26(1)(b), from any country: not held as an exchange list); 18 is the licence's own age. Section 26(5): a licence or renewal stays in force for a minimum of 12 months and up to 3 years; the form holds one term, so validYears is null (the range isn't a single number). Fee: the Regulations' schedule gives 'Licence or renewal of licence to drive motor vehicle $15' (Australian dollars, Nauru's currency), one fee whatever the term, held; the learner's permit is $7.50 (not held). The three 2024 amending regulations change only registration plates. No identity card is issued under the Act.
